$comment: The shrink-only STORY ratchet (#74), in the same shape as expected-parts.json.
scripts/run-axe-storybook.js refuses only a GLOBALLY empty story set. Nothing required any
particular story to exist, so a component shipping one `Default` story reported axe-zero
over one state and the gate could not tell that from full coverage. NFR-003 named that
defect in its own sentence — 'a component whose only story is its default state has had one
of its states tested' — and then supplied no mechanism that closed it.
This is the mechanism. Every story id listed here must exist in the built Storybook index;
a missing one fails the gate by name. Adding stories is free. REMOVING one requires editing
this file, which is the point: #74 deletes nothing, but it replaces eight hand-written
form-state HTML strings with element state, and the criterion that would have noticed their
loss was the one that could not.
Scoped to the ELEMENTS, not the whole catalogue. The thirteen packages/styles story files
predate this and pinning them here would be a ratchet nobody agreed to; #77-#79 migrate them
and can opt each in as it lands.

#78 opts sk-feature-card and sk-ribbon-card in. The a11y gate is what caught this batch's slotted-content contrast defect, and it is the ONLY gate that would catch a recurrence — so retiring these stories must not be silent. A lens noted four migrated elements were sitting outside this ratchet. These two are now in; sk-grid and sk-section-banner (#77's) are STILL OUTSIDE and are not covered by '#79 adds its own' — they need opting in by whoever touches them next.

#177 opts sk-card in, seventeen stories. It predated this ratchet, and the mission adds the stories the ratchet exists to protect — Greyscale and ForcedColors are the ONLY evidence that a status tone is not the sole carrier of meaning, and StatusCardComposition is the mission's proof that no sk-status-card element is needed. Retiring any of them must not be silent. Docs entries are excluded, matching every other element here.

#79 opts in its own three. The previous note said sk-grid and sk-section-banner were still outside and 'not covered by #79 adds its own' — two lenses observed #79 then added none either, so this per-component chore had been skipped by two batches running. FIVE element story files remain outside, not three: an earlier revision of this note said 'sk-card, sk-grid and sk-section-banner remain outside' and undercounted by two. The full list is sk-card, sk-grid, sk-section-banner, sk-nav-pill and sk-stub. sk-stub is the synthetic probe component and is arguably exempt, but nothing here said so, and a reader acting on the old count would have left two migrated elements silently unratcheted.

#78 opts sk-blog-card in: five ids, total 43 -> 48. Recorded because this is the ratchet a lens found gaining data silently while behaviours.json, expected-parts.json, mutations.json and expected-inert-theme-wrappers.json each recorded why they moved — and because the note above enumerates which element story files remain OUTSIDE, so a reader had no way to tell blog-card had been opted in. With blog-card in, the five still outside are sk-card, sk-grid, sk-section-banner, sk-nav-pill and sk-stub.

#77 opts sk-site-footer in: two ids, total 48 -> 50. With it in, the elements still outside this ratchet are sk-card, sk-grid, sk-section-banner, sk-nav-pill and sk-stub — unchanged, since this mission owns only site-footer. The `--docs` entry Storybook generates from the autodocs tag is not listed: it is a generated page, not a story, and no other element records one.

The three ForcedColorsBaseline decoy stories the pre-merge gate found (byte-identical renders of a sibling story, asserting a media state the axe harness never enters) were deleted before this ratchet was written, not opted in -- 21 is the real per-story count, not 24.

#182 adds seven for sk-page-header: 100 -> 107. Compact; Compact beside Default from identical slot content; a compact sticky header over a long scrolling fixture whose rows carry the documented scroll margin; the narrow reflow; the short-viewport drop; long title and long metadata truncating at compact density; and a compact sticky LightMode wrapped in `class="sk-light"`, never `data-theme`. The four ids #145 declared are unchanged.

#182, reviewer round: +1 for sk-page-header, 107 -> 108. DefaultSticky is a sticky header at the DEFAULT density — a supported combination the first pass shipped no story for, which is why apps/storybook/src/tests/sk-page-header-sticky.spec.ts's WCAG 2.4.11 assertion only ever ran against compact and the 64px published scroll margin went unchallenged against a measured 227-533px header. The story carries the documented remedy (the consumer overriding the token) so the assertion covers the configuration that previously failed.

#178 opts sk-notice in with all TWENTY of its stories, so every one is inside the axe gate rather than only the ones a reviewer thought to name. Three are load-bearing beyond coverage: `message-change` is the mission's own defect shown as a working affordance, `dismissible` shows the notice still present after the event it emitted, and `forced-colors` is deliberately NOT a re-render of `all-tones` — it adds a dismissible sample so the focus ring is in the frame, because #176's gate deleted three decoy forced-colors stories that rendered identically to a sibling and asserted nothing.

#219 opts in the FIRST styles-layer story: `components-card--statuses-greyscale`, one id, total 180 -> 181. The scope sentence four notes above — "scoped to the ELEMENTS, not the whole catalogue" because the packages/styles story files predate this and "#77-#79 migrate them and can opt each in as it lands" — has outlived its reason: those migrations landed and nothing was opted in. What replaces it is narrower than "everything" and stronger than "nothing": THE SCOPE IS THE ELEMENTS, PLUS ANY STORY A MISSION HAS NAMED AS ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE. The principle, stated so the next mission does not re-derive it: a story cited as proof is ratcheted in the same commit that cites it. This id specifically, because #177's implementation-evidence.md names `Greyscale` AND `StatusesGreyscale` as its proof that a status tone is never the sole carrier of meaning. The element-layer half (elements-skcard--greyscale) was ratcheted by that mission; the STATIC half was not — and the static path is the no-JavaScript consumer ADR-10 section 3 exists to serve, so it is the half where a reader has no element to fall back on. The story your evidence names as proof was, for the static layer, the one that could be retired silently. NOT the whole packages/styles catalogue, deliberately: #219 raises that as an open question and it is a larger scope decision than a follow-up mission should take. The sweep that bounds this: kitty-specs holds exactly ONE implementation-evidence.md today (card-status-tone-axis-01M1VJNY), and it cites exactly one styles-layer story. When a second mission cites one, it adds it here, in its own commit.
